note: n.. = the narrator (af_heart). a.. = the police artist (a male Kokoro voice, auditioned with task=cast on his own lines). Lines ending in b are variants of the line before, for the ears to choose between; only one of each pair is placed.
ref_text: The station is quiet in the afternoon. A fan turns, a pencil scratches on paper, and somebody down the corridor is asking for tea.

lines.text: You're the only one who saw the thief's face,
for about one second.
Quick, before he fades.
Round face, or long?
You don't know, so you guess.
Round.
Round, then.
And the mole. Which cheek?
This one.
That's him?
You cannot say it isn't.
You can't say it isn't.
Now pick him.
Whoever you pick goes to jail.
Chose number four? You chose the drawing, and so did the police: he's only here because he looks like it.
lines.text_kokoro: Chose number four? You chose the [drawing](/dɹˈɔːɪŋ/), and so did the police: he's only here because he looks like it.

lines.text: Picked number four? You picked the drawing, and so did the police: he's only here because he looks like it.
lines.text_kokoro: Picked number four? You picked the [drawing](/dɹˈɔːɪŋ/), and so did the police: he's only here because he looks like it.

lines.text: But the man you saw
is number two.
Chose him? You were right, and nobody believed you: he doesn't look like the drawing.
lines.text_kokoro: Chose him? You were right, and nobody believed you: he doesn't look like the [drawing](/dɹˈɔːɪŋ/).

lines.text: Picked him? You were right, and nobody believed you: he doesn't look like the drawing.
lines.text_kokoro: Picked him? You were right, and nobody believed you: he doesn't look like the [drawing](/dɹˈɔːɪŋ/).

lines.text: So number four goes to jail for two of your guesses, because a pencil cannot draw "not sure".
So number four goes to jail for two of your guesses, because no pencil can draw "not sure".
In nineteen eighty-four, a tip told police that Kirk Bloodsworth looked like their sketch.
lines.text_kokoro: In nineteen eighty-four, a tip told police that Kirk [Bloodsworth](/blˈʌdzwəɹθ/) looked like their sketch.

lines.text: DNA freed him more than eight years later.
And number two? He's having chai under a picture of your guess.
